clue.text: Hard work and energy, with erratic bowler's age

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: erratic means wandering or irregular, so the letters of these words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler, wild and getting on in years, still puts in hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' scrambles the ten letters of the two words, apostrophe ignored. In cricket the bowler delivers the ball to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for vigorous physical effort, such as scrubbing or polishing, is this hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: The queen must keep a home deposit

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the queen's letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: The monarch is told to keep a deposit paid on a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' tempts as part of a house-buying definition, but it is a bird's nest; 'deposit' alone defines, in the old sense of earnest money.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a sum paid in advance to bind a bargain, a deposit or pledge.

clue.text: Part of bathroom offer best regularly used

parts.note: to bid is to make an offer, as at an auction

indicators.note: using letters at regular intervals takes every other one of the word best

explanation.surface: A shopping instruction: put in a bid for bathroom fittings, using the best ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly used' takes the second and fourth letters of BEST, E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin for washing, found beside the toilet in many bathroom suites.

clue.text: Cover up heavy defeat

definitions.meaning: to conceal faults or wrongdoing, a political term for hushing something up
in sport, a crushing defeat in which the losers score nothing or win no games

explanation.surface: A sports report: officials hid the truth about a crushing loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime paint covers stains, giving the sense of concealment; in sport the word means a one-sided rout.

clue.text: Downright repulsive

explanation.surface: Something utterly disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both complete or utter, and foul or offensive in smell.

clue.text: 4 may be unqualified

definitions.meaning: the answer to 4 down means downright or utter, which this word can also mean

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying an earlier answer might lack any qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 4 is RANK, and 'rank nonsense' is 'utter' or 'total' nonsense, so rank is an example of the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete, total and without conditions: an unqualified success is an utter success.

clue.text: Put up before court after vacation

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: to vacate is to empty, so only the outside letters of court remain once its middle has gone

explanation.surface: A legal note: a case was put up for hearing before the court after the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after vacation' empties COURT to CT. 'Vacation' looks like the legal term for the courts' holiday but is the emptying signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a building or tent is to put it up, construct or raise it.

clue.text: Exercises underpinning poorly rated bureaucracy

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece that underpins sits below the other
done poorly, these letters are put in a bad, disordered arrangement

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Gym sessions supporting a badly regarded civil service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' scrambles RATED into REDTA, and PE goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official rules and forms, named after the tape once used to bind government papers.

clue.text: Cheese may be everything — and nothing in mostly damp environment

indicators.note: one piece is placed in another
the trimmed word forms the surroundings, the environment, for the other letters
mostly means all but the last letter of the word for damp

parts.note: humid means damp, of the air
all means everything
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Cheese might be everything, or nothing, when kept somewhere a bit damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final letter of the damp word; 'in' and 'environment' together signal the insertion, the trimmed word surrounding the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm, salty Cypriot cheese made from goat's and sheep's milk, often grilled.

clue.text: Two soldiers among Liverpool fans perhaps must be stars

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed among, inside, the other

parts.note: Liverpool FC are known as the Reds, as are their supporters
a GI is a US soldier and an ant can be a soldier ant, giving GI then ANT

explanation.surface: Two soldiers in a crowd of Liverpool supporters turn out to be celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities but means astronomical ones. Liverpool Football Club play in red and are nicknamed the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: Large, cool, late-stage stars that have swollen after using up their core hydrogen.

clue.text: Horned animal seen in European country

parts.note: land means a country, as in a foreign land

explanation.surface: A horned creature spotted in a country of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is only a link; nothing is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African antelope with spiral horns, the biggest of its kind.

clue.text: Last of Close Encounters reflected high opinion

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Close is used
a reflection reverses an image, so the word for encounters is read backwards

parts.note: meets means encounters

explanation.surface: The end of the film Close Encounters earned critics' high opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses the word for encounters. Close Encounters of the Third Kind is a Spielberg film, so 'Close' looks like part of a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard or respect: to hold someone in high regard is to think well of them.

clue.text: Charge including many a collection of boats

indicators.note: the first word includes, holds inside, the second

parts.note: to charge a glass or pipe is to fill it
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A fee covering a great deal for a group of vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' signals the insertion; the 'a' looks part of the definition but supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet or group of ships or small vessels sailing together.

clue.text: Headgear graduate used during performance

indicators.note: a piece used during another sits inside it

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate wore a piece of headgear during the show.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a music-hall or variety act, hence a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A long cloth wound around the head, worn especially by Sikh men.

clue.text: Remaining rule said to be reviewed

indicators.note: something reviewed is gone over and revised, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A regulation that remains in place is reported to be up for review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reviewed' rearranges RULE SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Left over at the end of a process, as a leftover amount or residue is.

clue.text: Approach height needing time for line

indicators.note: the word for height needs a new letter in place of one
one letter stands in for another, replacing it

parts.note: altitude means height

explanation.surface: An aircraft approach at height needs timing rather than a straight line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing ... for' swaps the L of ALTITUDE for T.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of thinking about something, a stance or outlook, as in one's approach to life.

clue.text: Differences in pitch offering breaks in play

definitions.meaning: in music, the gap between two notes
pauses between parts of a play or concert

explanation.surface: A theatre programme note on changes of pitch offering pauses in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Musically, the steps between notes; in the theatre, the pauses between acts.

clue.text: 'Horse's heart found in cooking pot' — bold headline

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other

parts.note: a steamer is a pot for steaming food

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, here the central letter of horse

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline: a horse's heart found in a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes R, the middle letter of HORSE; 'found in' puts it inside STEAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism, a headline running across the full width of a page, also called a banner.

clue.text: Lover of beauty hates to move before summer in Nice

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

parts.note: été is French for summer, Nice being a French city

explanation.surface: An art lover hates to leave until after the summer in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges HATES into AESTH, then ETE, French for summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with refined sensitivity to art and beauty, sometimes to excess.

clue.text: Contract could be a game of cards

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A deal in bridge is a contract, so this reads as a card-table remark.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the 'contract' is the bid a side undertakes to make, so the verb is misdirected as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, to make it contract.

clue.text: Removes blunders by head of security

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of security

parts.note: trips are stumbles or blunders

explanation.surface: The security chief takes away people's mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip something is to take it off or away, as in stripping paint or clothes.

clue.text: Questionable view to have leader replaced by revolutionary American

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for view is swapped for the next piece

parts.note: an aspect is a view or outlook

indicators.note: revolving turns the letters round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A doubtful opinion, held once a revolutionary American takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns US into SU, which replaces the A of ASPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Of doubtful reliability or honesty, open to question, as suspect evidence is.

clue.text: Run courses about adult salad ingredients

indicators.note: the outer letters go about, around, the next piece

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
dishes are courses of a meal
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A menu note: run the courses round an adult's salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside R + DISHES, just after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Small red peppery root vegetables, eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Lad in charge of sound waves

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A boy put in charge of sound engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things relating to sound and its waves, as in a sonic boom.

clue.text: Crikey, I'm not sure British Standard is applied to credit

indicators.note: the following pieces are applied, attached, after the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
um is a hesitant noise when not sure
BS is the abbreviation for British Standard

explanation.surface: An exclamation of uncertainty about whether a quality mark applies to credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of surprise, like gosh or good heavens.

clue.text: State colliery must contain answer

indicators.note: the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A rule that a coal pit must contain the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must contain' puts A inside MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in New England, the most north-easterly of the forty-eight mainland states.

clue.text: Father on African Union married woman in Germany

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest's view on the African Union's wife in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for a wife, and the title Mrs.

clue.text: Sketched daybreak across river

indicators.note: the word for daybreak lies across, spanning, the next letter

parts.note: dawn is daybreak

explanation.surface: An artist sketched the sunrise over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside DAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle of draw, to make a picture with pencil or pen.

clue.text: Spread grain out to be eaten by horse

indicators.note: a thing eaten goes inside the eater, so these letters sit within the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: out signals letters knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Instructions to put grain out for a horse to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the grain; 'to be eaten by' places those letters inside the female horse. 'Spread' looks like a verb but is the noun for what goes on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter substitute made from vegetable oils, spread on bread.

clue.text: Cautious male in big top maybe kissed, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is said aloud, so these pieces sound like the answer

parts.words: male in big top maybe kissed
parts.note: M for male goes inside CIRCUS, a big top being a circus tent, then PECKED for kissed

explanation.surface: A man in a circus tent, perhaps kissed, ought to be wary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the insertion within the spoken piece; 'we hear' says the built phrase is only said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wary and careful to consider all risks before acting, prudent.
